  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality and
integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain from
abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which we
have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create a
perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest in
thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

ITEM NO. 3  ATTENDANCE POLICY
ATTENDANCE POLICY

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez presented the report.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo noted that young people may also suffer from chronic
  issues, and that they should be able to have their absences excused,
  to which Director Rodriguez stated that the policy permits excusing
  said absences.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez clarified that the subject policy covers activities
  and not field trips, as these are covered under another policy.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman voiced concern over requiring 72-hour notices
ROMAN  of absences, noting that becoming sick over a holiday weekend may
  not give individuals sufficient time to cancel their attendance at an
  event. She also spoke about how absences from programs such as
  cheer affect the other participants and opposed requiring
  documentation confirming illnesses.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo suggested that the policy reflect that it is subject to change
  depending on local / state emergency orders and requirements.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ In response to a comment by Chair Fraijo, Director Rodriguez
  indicated that the subject policy would only cover programs and
  activities that have waiting lists and noted that staff is required to follow
  local occupancy and fire codes. She added that some programs have
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 6, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 3

  children that sincerely wish to participate but cannot do so while on
  the wait list, while other children that have been accepted into the
  program do not regularly attend, and in doing so, they deny the
  participation of the children on the wait list.

  Responding to a question by Chair Fraijo, Director Rodriguez advised
  that she would address appeals.

  Chair Fraijo requested to be provided a full report on the feedback
  received to the policy, if enacted, and requested that the policy clearly
  address chronic health issues and a statement indicating that the
  policy is subject to change.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez stressed that staff does not desire to remove
  children from participating in programs, and staff is cognizant of the
  circumstances behind some of the children’s absences.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo suggested potentially reaching out to parents whose
  children routinely miss classes in an attempt to assist and enable more
  regular attendance.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda asked about how the policy would apply to Senior
  Center programs, which Director Rodriguez elaborated on. Dena
  Zepeda commended staff for their concern for children and for their
  regular communication with their parents.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ In response to a comment by Dena Zepeda, Director Rodriguez noted
  that the Senior Commission has already provided input on the
  proposed policy.

MEGAN ZEPEDA  Megan Zepeda made a suggestion for the policy.

MOTION  A motion was made by Commissioner Roman, seconded by
  Commissioner Duran, to recommend changes to the proposed
  Attendance Policy, including the removal of the requirement of the
  submittal of doctor’s notes, adding chronic illnesses as excused
  absences, that the policy would be subject to local emergencies, and
  that the policy be reviewed after one year. The motion was
  unanimously approved.

ITEM NO. 9  PRIDE MONTH EVENTS – VERBAL REPORT
PRIDE MONTH EVENTS

MANAGER ZEPEDA  Manager Zepeda presented the report.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo requested that staff present ideas for a future Pride Month

 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 6, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 9

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman stated that the Council had previously
ROMAN  discussed ways to recognize Pride Month and that it had determined

  people’s sexual orientations. She further stated that a previous
  suggestion to hold a parade is not desired by anyone and expressed

  inappropriate might be displayed at such a parade.

  requests, and that individuals are free to choose whether or not to
  participate.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman stated that she has received comments from
ROMAN  parents who feel that Pride events are being imposed on them. She
  added that Pride events can display nudity and other inappropriate
  things. She suggested perhaps scheduling a trip to a Pride event
  outside the city next June.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo stated that such an event would not be overwhelming or
  inappropriate. The Commission could consider it and make a
  recommendation to the City Council.

MEGAN ZEPEDA  Megan Zepeda stated that she enjoys drag shows but would not want
  children exposed to Pride events.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Duran agreed that a trip would probably be a good
DURAN  place to start. She also commented about promoting inclusion.
  However, she stated that Pride events have no place in the
  community, nor should it be a Recreation Department event.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo stated that the City can offer a trip where anyone can
  participate and, if it is not successful, it would be discontinued, which
  is the same process for all other programs and activities.

LINDA MAREZ  Linda Marez stated that Irwindale doesn’t single out individuals.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Ortiz stated that she is not looking to be in the spotlight
ORTIZ  and is instead attempting to help children similar to her feel welcome.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 6, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 10
